LIVERPOOL, England, Oct 17 : Chelsea beat Everton 2-0 in the Premier League on Saturday thanks to a double from Pedro Neto as the London club provisionally moved up to fourth in a game overshadowed by an injury to goalkeeper Emi Martinez. After a goalless but feisty first half that produced five yellow cards and several heated exchanges, Chelsea needed just 43 seconds after the restart to go 1-0 up when an unmarked Neto swept home. The game was paused for several minutes when Chelsea's Martinez was taken off on a stretcher following a collision with Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite, with 21-year-old keeper Mike Penders coming on for his Premier League debut. Chelsea doubled their lead in the 90th minute when Neto pounced on a loose ball after Jordan Henderson's free kick was blocked by the wall, finding the bottom corner with a composed finish as Everton suffered their first defeat of the season.

Source: Reuters

NEW DELHI: India's "cockroach" youth movement leader was released by an Indian court on Saturday (Oct 17), a day after he was detained for trying to lead another protest rally in New Delhi calling for the resignation of the country's election chief. Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), rose to prominence this year when a weeks-long sit-in contributed to India's education minister resigning. CJP's legal affairs head Ratna Singh said Dipke was released after he agreed to certain conditions. Singh gave no details of the terms. Dipke's youth-led group, opposition parties and student organisations have held near-daily protests this month demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over a revision of voter lists that they say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

More than 130 million voters were deleted during the revision. The Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol. The BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes. Student activist Neha Bora, a prominent face of the protests, who was also detained on Friday as she tried to reach central Delhi with dozens of supporters, was released on Saturday. "Please, spare the people of India. Impeach Gyanesh Kumar and halt SIR (special intensive revision), so that the ordinary citizens of this country can breathe a sigh of relief, feel at ease, and have their voting rights ensured," Bora told ANI news agency after she was released.

STUDENT GROUPS CALL FOR MORE PROTEST ACTION Dipke was detained on Friday as he stepped out of a house in central Delhi, with police hauling him into a police car and driving away after a brief argument. Dipke had called Friday's protest in support of two CJP leaders detained and sent to jail this week for five days for demonstrating at a protest site in violation of a ban. Earlier on Friday, police had met Dipke and warned him against going ahead with the protest. Student groups called for more protest action on Saturday. The movement, which was mobilised by the youth and joined by many opposition parties, has emerged as one of the biggest political challenges faced by Modi and the BJP in the prime minister's 12 years in power.

Source: Reuters/dy

Oct 17 : South Africa have not yet confirmed their playing XI for the second test against Australia which starts in Gqeberha on Sunday as they assess the likely impact of the weather on the game and consider playing two spinners again. The home side were beaten by 214 runs in the first test of the three-match series in Durban and need to improve with both bat and ball as they seek put pressure on the tourists. Captain Temba Bavuma confirmed on Saturday that the team were still mulling over several options for their playing personnel. “We would like to see what happens tomorrow,” he told reporters. “Whether we go with two spinners is probably one of the biggest considerations.

FAST

BANGKOK, Oct 17 : Rapidly improving artificial intelligence capabilities will bring far faster change across all fields, Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark said on Saturday, with one of the company's internal models forecasting that under certain conditions it could increase US economic output by almost 50 per cent by 2030. Clark, speaking at IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, said that international cooperation was needed to erect "unusual and serious rules" for the transformative technology, and there was a shrinking window for policymakers to act. Clark said that the estimated potential US GDP of $44 trillion, which compares to the current level of just over $30 trillion, "sounds very outlandish, I know." But he added that AI was vastly increasing scientific discovery. He said the forecast assumed "the technology continuing to get better. And if GDP were to grow this much, then economic doctrine suggests that new industries and inventions would need to have been created to power such a major economic expansion".

Clark's remarks come as the company prepares for an initial public offering expected in November that could value the firm at up to $2 trillion.  HUMANS IN CONTROL, FOR NOW Clark issued a wake-up call to policymakers about the speed of AI development, saying there was growing evidence of a "singularity" where AI development outpaces human control. "We should expect that in the coming years, the whole pace of progress of not just AI but science as a whole will speed up, and this will feel confusing and disorienting, and will bring with it great wealth and potentially great peril," he said in a lecture to hundreds of government and finance officials. AI was a major topic at the IMF and World Bank meetings, as both a source of growth offsetting high energy prices and a potential threat to stability if it falls short of its promise as a productivity game-changer and stock valuations crash.  Officials also expressed worries about AI destroying certain jobs and leaving some countries behind. But Clark, a former journalist who serves as Anthropic's "head of public benefit," painted a picture of a rosy future where AI was a force multiplier for scientific discovery, solving mathematical, engineering and biological problems, including new drug discovery, as human researchers are supplemented by hundreds or thousands of AI assistants.  More countries can participate in the AI revolution by helping to build the data center computing capacity needed to power AI, he said. STRICTEST CONTROLS ON BIOLOGICAL RESEARCH Clark cautioned that global leaders need to understand how powerful AI will become and make urgent choices about how to regulate the technology. "Being able to use AI for science opens us up to the misuses of science as well, biological and cyber weapons and things we cannot yet imagine, and we have many choices to make," he said. Biological research, where AI has already created new viruses, is an area "where we want the strictest human oversight and transparency to maintain safety." Despite some recent high-profile incidents where rogue AI systems have escaped testing environments and hacked websites and databases, he said AI was still under human control. But the window to impose safeguards was shrinking as AI became more capable and was now "a small number of years."  Clark also acknowledged that AI was causing job losses in some fields with "high AI exposure" such as call centers and customer service personnel. But for other fields, such as scientific research, he said AI was enhancing employment and a major unknown was its potential to create jobs in completely new industries.

Source: Reuters

FAST

SYDNEY, Oct 17 : New Zealand coach Dave Rennie said his team would be sticking to their expansive style at next year's World Cup after the All Blacks thrashed the Wallabies for a second successive week with some sensational attacking rugby on Saturday.  Two convincing wins over Australia have got the three-times world champions back to winning ways after they lost a four-match series against South Africa 3-1.  The Springboks have ridden a physical, conservative playing style to back-to-back World Cup triumphs but Rennie said he remained convinced the tactics that put a premium on ball speed and width would be effective against it.  "There's no point playing this way and then going to a World Cup and trying to play risk-free footy," he told reporters after the 42-21 victory at Stadium Australia.

"We're well aware you can put yourself under pressure the way that we're trying to play, but we'll also back ourselves that we'll profit more than we'll suffer in those situations.  "I don't think you want all the teams in the world playing the same game. I think if you look at the Wallabies, they're pretty similar to us. I think they'll want to play, and it's a point of difference, part of the DNA of both sides."  "If you want to just get into arm wrestles with a couple of the big sides in the world, it'll be a struggle," he said.   Despite his team scoring six tries with some breathtaking rugby in the first half on Saturday, Rennie said there were still improvements to be made.  "We're trying to grow our game, and we've got a long way to go," he said.  "We just want to be able to play at a tempo that will test other sides."  Australia coach Les Kiss said he was pleased with the performance of flyhalf Declan Meredith in only his fourth test and remained confident the Wallabies could put on a good showing at their home World Cup next year.    "I've always said we'll have ups and downs, and today it was a bit of a downer again," he said.  "But there are some good clues about what we're trying to do in our game. When we do play with footy in the hand with a positive intent, we're making a lot of breaks against one of the best teams in the world.  "So I think there are some good qualities that are coming through. So I'm optimistic still."

FAST

SYDNEY, Oct 17 : The All Blacks rode a first-half try blitz to a 43-21 victory over the Wallabies at Stadium Australia on Saturday, extending their win streak over their trans-Tasman-Sea rivals to 13 matches.  With the Bledisloe Cup already safely in the cupboard for a 24th year after last week's 50-19 win in Auckland, New Zealand exploded out of the blocks and crushed all thoughts of an upset with six tries before the break.  Despite losing Jordie Barrett to a calf injury before kickoff and another centre in Quinn Tupaea early on with a concussion, the All Blacks overwhelmed the Wallabies with power, pace and precision in the opening 40 minutes. "I'm really proud of the boys, the way we came out on that in that first half," said New Zealand captain Codie Taylor.

"It was a real challenge for us this week to make sure that we backed up a really good performance from last week, and I thought we were awesome in that first 40." Australia showed some flashes of backline brilliance, particularly in the second half, but struggled to get hold of the ball for prolonged periods and were unable to match the accuracy or clinical finishing of the All Blacks.    In a whirlwind of offloads, winger Josh Moorby, fullback Beauden Barrett, flanker Peter Lakai and replacement back Rieko Ioane all crossed in the first 26 minutes to give the visitors a quick-fire 22-0 lead.  Wallabies flyhalf Declan Meredith did well to get a pass away in the tackle just before the half-hour mark to send Jeremy Williams over for a try but the lock was sin-binned at the other end of the field two minutes later.  All Blacks number eight Wallace Sititi immediately made the extra man count with his team's fifth try and Beauden Barrett added a sixth, his second, off an intercept to send New Zealand into the break with a 36-7 lead. Moorby faked out the defence for his second five-pointer within three minutes of the restart before the Wallabies finally finished off a backline move for fullback Tom Wright to go over.  Australia were looking stronger with their replacements on the pitch, and Meredith almost scored a try after a scything break up the middle, then saved a try at the other end. A clever line dropout from Wright did result in a third Australia try in the 66th minute for replacement back Filipo Daugunu that delighted the majority of the crowd of 73,399.    New Zealand were reduced to 14 men after Samisoni Taukei'aho went off injured, and went down to 13 when debutant Chay Fihaki was shown a yellow card but managed to hold out the Wallabies for the last few minutes. "I'm gutted," said Wallabies captain Harry Wilson. "When you give a team like the All Blacks a head start it's tough, and it's not good enough for this group. "We've got to be a lot better. It's been a very disappointing series, and we're going to have to regroup."

Source: Reuters

Oct 17 : Mahela Jayawardene has stepped down from his role as the Mumbai Indians head coach, the Indian Premier League (IPL) team said on Saturday. In his first stint at Mumbai Indians from 2017 to 2022, the 49-year-old guided the side to three titles. However, the former Sri Lanka captain was not able to replicate that success after rejoining the side in 2024, with Mumbai Indians finishing fourth in 2025 and losing in the playoffs, before ending the league second-bottom in 2026. "Together, we have shared some unforgettable moments, overcome challenges and built something we can all be proud of," Jayawardene said in a statement. "I leave with immense pride in what we have achieved together and will always carry a special place in my heart for MI. I wish the team every success in the years ahead."

Source: Reuters

Oct 16 : American Brandon Figueroa has been stripped of his WBA featherweight title after hitting the scales 1.4 pounds over the 126-pound weight limit for Saturday's fight against Tomoki Kameda of Japan, organisers said on Friday. Kameda, 35, will be able to clinch the vacant title if he wins the fight, which will go ahead as scheduled in Las Vegas. "Honestly, it's disrespectful, because I'm here, I suffered too. I did my thing. I'm ready for tomorrow," Kameda said, speaking via a translator. "It has been 18 months since I fought, but look at me, look how shredded I am. You know I'm ready. Everything remains the same, I'm going for the title tomorrow."

MANILA, Oct 17 : Multilateral development banks (MDBs) will strengthen efforts to help mineral-rich developing economies add more value to their resources by moving beyond extraction into processing, refining and manufacturing, according to an outline of a critical minerals collaboration framework published on Saturday. • The banks involved include the World Bank, the African Development Bank, the Asian Development Bank, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the European Investment Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank, according to the outline • The October framework calls for coordinated support across critical mineral supply chains, including financing, infrastructure and policy aimed at creating jobs, boosting domestic value addition, attracting private investment and supporting low-carbon transition • MDBs plan to support mineral corridors incorporating power, transport, logistics, water and digital infrastructure, while strengthening project preparation and using co-financing, guarantees and other financing tools to mobilise capital and accelerate private sector investments

Oct 17 : Former Giro d'Italia winner and Olympic champion Richard Carapaz joined NSN Cycling Team on Friday, after leaving EF Education-EasyPost a year before the end of his contract. The 33-year-old Ecuadorean, who won the Giro in 2019 and road race gold at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, signed a three-year deal with NSN, formerly known as Israel–Premier Tech. "I'm really looking forward to it, and to be honest, this reminds me a lot of when I signed my first professional contract, when I was incredibly excited about being in the WorldTour," Carapaz said in a statement. "The team has big ambitions to keep growing and already in my conversations with the performance team, it was clear we share the same desire to keep improving and achieve big things together." Carapaz, renowned for his climbing ability, won two stages at this year's Tour de France to finish eighth overall.
